note: Item codes are the deposit's own column names: data/kay_2025.R selects starts_with('cf_') from OSF uzrgk data_deidentified.csv (z28r4) and pivots cols 4:14 with names kept, no resp shift (raw 1..7; deposit reproduces live per-item n=492, means and floor/ceiling exactly). Wording transcribed verbatim from the study's own Qualtrics printout 'Qualtrics Survey (Time 1).pdf' (au83k, block page_4); the task is not in the Time 2 printout (q9m27), consistent with live data having no wave. Unlike the Likert blocks in this battery, the printout prints the ten sequences with EMPTY export tags '()', so cf_specific_<k> is the Qualtrics matrix row id and the tie of k to sequence is by printed order (paper_order); no .qsf is on the node (8 files listed via OSF API) and neither authors' Rmd (5a3gc, x65ja) names individual sequences. Checked by Step 5b route 4 (streakiness implied by the text): the 4 highest-mean codes are exactly the 4 sequences with a run of >=5 (1/210 under a random permutation) and the single run-6 sequence (HHHHHHTHHT) is code 3, the highest mean; within the balanced sequences 4-9 and between 1 and 10 order rests on the printout alone. cf_overall_1 is its own question (tag cf_overall, row 'All 100 throws above'), unambiguous. item_text is the printed sequence string / row label; the matrix question stems go in section_prompt per section (cf_specific prompt for _1, cf_overall prompt for _2) since they differ, instructions blank. Printout anchors only the endpoints: 1 = 'Completely Random', 7 = 'Completely Determined'; 2-6 are bare numbers and are left blank. Quotes are straight as printed. The ten sequences are NOT the examples van Prooijen et al. (2018) print ('HTHHTTTTHH', 'HHHTTTTTHH'), and the overall prompt is reworded from theirs; Kay & Slovic's own stimuli, though like the original they total 50 H / 50 T. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv CoinToss-IPP row, verdict ship (Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381 R12, origin van Prooijen et al. 2018 CC BY), applied not re-derived.
